options_en: Sirti — Emergency military cess during wartime
Maro — Escheat/property seizure upon the death of a sonless person
Baikar — Tax collected in the form of food grains

extra_data.question_en: Which ruler of the Panwar dynasty of Garhwal conquered the 52 forts (Garhs) and established the standard measurement unit 'Dhuli Patha' and the 'Sarola Brahmin' system?
extra_data.explanation_en: Raja Ajaypal (37th ruler of the Panwar dynasty) unified the 52 scattered Garhs of Garhwal and shifted his capital to Devalgarh (1512) and then Srinagar (1517). extra_data.exam_name: UKSSSC High Court Junior Assistant / Stenographer
extra_data.question_en: With reference to the administrative reforms of G. W. Traill (1816–1835), the second British Commissioner of Kumaon, which statement is INCORRECT?
options_en: He conducted the first scientific land settlement (Beckett Settlement) in 1863
He carried out the 'Assi Saala Settlement' and boundary demarcations in 1823 CE
He created 9 Patwari posts in 1819 and established the Excise Department in 1822
He introduced the 'Double Lock System' in 1824 to safeguard the government treasury
extra_data.explanation_en: The first scientific land settlement based on cadastral survey and soil classification (the 9th settlement / Beckett Settlement) was conducted between 1863 and 1873 by J. O'B. Beckett during the tenure of Commissioner Henry Ramsay, not G. W. Traill. Traill introduced the famous 80-year (Assi Saala / 1823) settlement (Samvat 1880), the Patwari system in 1819, and the double lock treasury system in 1824.

extra_data.question_en: In which British land settlement in Uttarakhand was agricultural land categorized for the first time into 5 classes: Talaon, Upraon Awwal, Upraon Doyam, Ijran, and Katil?
extra_data.explanation_en: In the 9th Land Settlement (1863–1873) conducted by J. O'B. extra_data.question_en: The famous 'Gauna Lake' formed on the Birahi Ganga in Chamoli in 1893 due to a massive landslide breach was wiped out in which year's devastating flash floods?
extra_data.explanation_en: In September 1893, a massive rockslide blocked the Birahi Ganga (a tributary of Alaknanda in Chamoli), forming the Gauna Lake (Gohna Lake). After surviving partially for 77 years, the lake burst catastrophically during the severe Alaknanda deluge of 20 July 1970, washing away the natural reservoir and inundating downstream valleys.

options_en: Substituted 'internal disturbance' with 'armed rebellion'; barred suspension of Articles 20 and 21
Empowered the President to proclaim emergency solely on the oral advice of the Prime Minister
Extended the parliamentary approval deadline from 1 month to 6 months
extra_data.explanation_en: The 44th Amendment Act, 1978 replaced the vague term 'internal disturbance' with 'armed rebellion', made written recommendation of the Union Cabinet mandatory for proclaiming emergency, and ensured that fundamental rights under Article 20 (protection in respect of conviction for offences) and Article 21 (right to life and personal liberty) cannot be suspended during an emergency.

extra_data.question_en: With reference to the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), which statement is CORRECT?
options_en: It has 8 members in total and meets once a year
It consists of 6 members (3 from RBI + 3 appointed by Central Government); RBI Governor holds a casting vote in case of a tie
The target inflation band is set at 0% to 2%
The Union Finance Minister is the ex-officio Chairperson
extra_data.explanation_en: Under Section 45ZB of the RBI Act, 1934, the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) consists of 6 members: 3 from RBI (including the Governor as ex-officio Chairperson) and 3 external members appointed by the Central Government. In case of an equality of votes, the RBI Governor has a casting vote. The inflation target is 4% with a tolerance band of +/- 2% (2% to 6%).

extra_data.question_en: What is the correct formula for calculating 'Primary Deficit' in the Union Budget?
extra_data.explanation_en: Primary Deficit is defined as Fiscal Deficit minus Interest Payments: Primary Deficit = Fiscal Deficit - Interest Payments. It indicates the borrowing requirements of the government solely to meet current operational expenses, excluding past accumulated interest liabilities.

extra_data.question_en: Rohit walks 12 km North, then turns right and walks 8 km, and then turns right again and walks 6 km. In which direction and at what distance is he now from his starting point?
extra_data.explanation_en: Net North displacement = 12 - 6 = 6 km. Net East displacement = 8 km. Using the Pythagorean theorem: Distance = sqrt(6^2 + 8^2) = sqrt(36 + 64) = sqrt(100) = 10 km. The direction from the starting point is North-East.

extra_data.question_en: In operating systems, what is the precise meaning of 'Thrashing' and 'Deadlock'?
options_en: CPU constantly busy swapping pages in/out | Processes waiting endlessly for mutually held resources
Clearing cache memory | Forgetting BIOS password
extra_data.explanation_en: Thrashing occurs in virtual memory systems when excessive page swapping between RAM and secondary storage consumes virtually all CPU time, collapsing overall system performance. Deadlock is a state where two or more processes are permanently blocked because each process is holding a resource and waiting for another resource held by the other.

extra_data.question_en: Under Section 80 of the Code of Civil Procedure (CPC), 1908, what is the mandatory statutory notice period required before instituting a civil suit against the Government or a public officer in respect of an official act?
extra_data.explanation_en: Under Section 80(1) of the CPC, 1908, no suit shall be instituted against the Government or against a public officer in respect of any act purporting to be done in official capacity until the expiration of two months next after notice in writing has been delivered. extra_data.question_en: With reference to the High Court's writ jurisdiction under Article 226 and its power of superintendence under Article 227 of the Constitution, which statement is CORRECT?
options_en: The jurisdiction under Article 226 is narrower than that of Article 32
Armed Forces Tribunals are also subject to superintendence under Article 227
Article 226 covers enforcement of fundamental and ordinary legal rights; Article 227 confers both administrative and judicial superintendence over subordinate courts
Only administrative superintendence is permissible under Article 227, not judicial
extra_data.explanation_en: Under Article 226, High Courts can issue writs not only for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights but also for 'any other purpose' (ordinary legal rights), making its writ scope wider than Article 32. Article 227 gives the High Court both administrative and judicial superintendence over all courts and tribunals throughout its territorial jurisdiction (excluding armed forces tribunals under clause 4).

extra_data.question_en: What is the most salient structural reform introduced in the new 'Income Tax Act, 2025' enforced from 1 April 2026?
options_en: Abolition of mandatory individual income tax return filing
Elimination of 'Previous Year' and 'Assessment Year' replaced by a single 'Tax Year' (1 April–31 March)
Merger of direct taxes (Income Tax) and indirect taxes (GST) into a single code
Shift of the financial tax year to a calendar year (1 January to 31 December)
extra_data.explanation_en: The new Income Tax Act, 2025 simplified tax terminology by completely abolishing the age-old confusing dual concepts of 'Previous Year' (Financial Year in which income is earned) and 'Assessment Year' (subsequent year in which income is taxed), replacing both with a unified concept of 'Tax Year' running from 1 April to 31 March.
